text: Suppose single observations symmetric location-scale family. , \(\rho()\) symmetric density function PDF \(X\) \(\frac{1}{\sigma}\rho\left(\frac{X-\mu}{\sigma}\right)\) center \(\mu\) scale \(\sigma\). example, \(X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)\). Given prespecified value \(\), valid confidence intervals form \[ X \pm \eta |X - | \] \[ \frac{X + }{2} \pm \eta |X - | \] can constructed produce valid \((1 - \alpha)100\%\) confidence intervals. done making \(\eta\) large enough bound coverage probability \((1 - \alpha)\). See Blachman Machol (1987). function ci1() produces confidence intervals \(\rho()\) density () standard normal, (ii) Cauchy, (iii) uniform. Surprisingly, constructing intervals using uniform distribution makes valid \((1 - \alpha)100\%\) confidence intervals \(X\) unimodal density. Suppose observe \(X = 2\) use \(= 1\), , centered \(X\), various 95% intervals : Centered \((X + ) / 2\), interested, can get values \(\eta\) normal, Cauchy, uniform via wc_width(). E.g., normal distribution 95% confidence interval form \((X + )/2 \pm \eta|X-|\), value \(\eta\)

title: Introduction to nisone
text: Robert (1991) considered generalized inverse normal distribution form \[ f(x|\alpha,\mu,\tau) = K(\alpha,\mu,\tau)|x|^{-\alpha}\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2\tau^2}\left(\frac{1}{x}-\mu\right)^2\right\}, \] \(K(\alpha,\mu,\tau)\) proportionality constant. \(\alpha = 2\), corresponds inverse normal distribution (different inverse Gaussian distribution), \(\frac{1}{X} \sim N(\mu, \tau^2)\). generalized inverse normal distribution shows Bayesian analysis parameterize normal distribution terms mean \(\mu\) coefficient variation \(\nu = \mu / \tau\). nisone() R package contains density, distribution, quantile, random generation functions (generalized) inverse normal distribution. can use get full posterior distribution \(n=1\) intervals \(\rho()\) normal. normal case, marginal posterior \(\mu - \) inverse normal inverse mean \(\frac{1}{X - }\) inverse variance \(\frac{1}{(X - )^2}\). E.g., observed \(X = 2\) use \(= 0.75\), full posterior density  can get 95% Credible intervals via agree bci1() Interfacing posterior provided n1post functions don’t need manually calculate posterior . generally, functions generalized inverse normal.
code: museq <- seq(-2, 5, length.out = 500) X <- 2 A <- 0.75 density <- dinvnorm(x = museq - A, imean = 1 / (X - A), isd = 1 / abs(X - A)) graphics::plot(   museq,    density,   type = "l",   xlab = expression(mu),   ylab = "Posterior Density" ) qinvnorm(p = c(0.025, 0.975), imean = 1 / (X - A), isd = 1 / abs(X - A)) + A #> [1] -10.68877  13.44327 bci1(x = X, A = A) #>      x      med     lower    upper #> [1,] 2 1.637283 -10.68877 13.44327 dn1post(x = 10, obs = X, A = A, nu = 1, fam = "normal") #> [1] 0.004009705 dinvnorm(x = 10 - A, imean = 1 / (X - A), isd = 1 / abs(X - A)) #> [1] 0.004009705  qn1post(p = c(0.025, 0.975), A = A, obs = X, nu = 1, fam = "normal") #> [1] -10.68877  13.44327 qinvnorm(p = c(0.025, 0.975), imean = 1 / (X - A), isd = 1 / abs(X - A)) + A #> [1] -10.68877  13.44327 set.seed(50) qginvnorm(p = 0.025, alpha = 4, mu = 0.5, tau = 1) #> [1] -1.344991 pginvnorm(q = -1.345, alpha = 4, mu = 0.5, tau = 1) #> [1] 0.02499958 samp <- rginvnorm(n = 1000, alpha = 4, mu = 0.5, tau = 1) x <- seq(min(samp), max(samp), length.out = 500) y <- dginvnorm(x = x, alpha = 4, mu = 0.5, tau = 1) modes <- xginvnorm(alpha = 4, mu = 0.5, tau = 1) hist(   samp,   freq = FALSE,   breaks = 100,   xlab = "x",   main = "Generalized Inverse Normal Density") lines(x, y, col = "#E69F00") abline(v = modes, col = "#56B4E9", lty = 2)
